data.one_liner: Gets system proxy settings to configure HttpOverrides for Flutter apps.
data.what_it_does: The plugin reads the device's proxy configuration and creates an HttpOverrides object. You assign it to HttpOverrides.global so that the standard http package routes requests through the system proxy. It works on Android and iOS.
use_when: You need to route http package traffic through a debugging proxy like Charles or Fiddler
You want automatic use of the device's proxy settings without hard‑coding them
avoid_when: Your app does not use the http package (e.g., uses dio or graphql clients)
You target platforms without system proxy support (web, desktop)
strengths: Very small and easy to add
No extra native code or build steps
Works automatically with the built‑in http client
weaknesses: Only supports the http package; other clients need manual proxy config
Limited to Android and iOS platforms
No runtime API to change proxy after creation
data.setup_notes: Call HttpProxyOverride.createHttpProxy() and assign the result to HttpOverrides.global before runApp()

alternatives.name: dio
alternatives.why_pick_it: Dio lets you set a proxy directly in its Options, avoiding the need for a separate plugin
